transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... I just can't stop thinking about my appearance. I work as a host at a restaurant, and I'm constantly fixated on my hairline and how my face looks, especially under the harsh lights in the dining room. I just feel like they make me look really old and... strange. It takes up a lot of my thoughts. My coworkers tell me they don't see what I'm talking about at all, but I just can't stop focusing on it.
Do you find yourself performing any specific actions, like checking your reflection in mirrors or grooming yourself excessively, to try to fix or hide these features?

Yes, I do. Um, especially right before a shift. I'll just keep checking the bathroom mirror over and over. I take pictures on my phone from different angles to try to see exactly what I look like, and I'm always combing my hair forward to try and hide my hairline. I just keep replaying in my head how the guests might see me when I walk up to them. Honestly, it takes up so much time that I end up being late, or I get so worked up I can barely bring myself to go out to the front stand.

latest_inference.note: The patient's focus on a perceived flaw in their physical appearance that others do not observe, combined with repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, excessive grooming/camouflaging) and significant impairment in daily functioning, strongly points toward Body Dysmorphic Disorder, ruling out OCD and Delusional Disorder.
